dedupe_keys.name: port of virginia private 5g network at its container terminals verizon customer story

description: This customer story from Verizon Business describes how the Virginia Port Authority, which owns and operates the six terminals of The Port of Virginia, replaced a mix of Wi-Fi and VHF and UHF radio with a Verizon private 5G network. Coverage: the port handled 3.4 million TEU in financial year 2025, with more than 1.1 million containers by truck, 720,000 by rail and 75,000 by barge and 1,700 vessel calls. Stacks of containers up to 70 feet high blocked line of sight, taxi drivers used the licensed radio channels, and calls between truck drivers and terminal staff dropped, which the port saw as a safety issue in hurricanes and other severe weather. The network combines 5G Ultra Wideband small cells with an LTE packet core, on private licensed spectrum chosen over shared CBRS spectrum because of nearby US Navy and Coast Guard facilities; it has been in service since 2024. Format and access: a web page. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: a vendor account without performance measurements. The design choices (licensed spectrum, small cells among container stacks) can inform telecom dependency and coverage assumptions in port operations and resilience models. It relates to the NASCTN CBRS spectrum sharing assessment and the DataPorts demonstrations in the catalogue.
